page: Microsoft Azure B16pls_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the Bpsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The architecture is arm64, with a cache configuration of 64 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable, and it does not include any GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across most workloads, with some specific weaknesses. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score is 1822.69, and the multi-core score is 28890.73, both falling into the average category. Geekbench testing shows a weak single-core score of 1102.0 but an average multi-core score of 9532.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1126.95 GB/sec for cached small blocks, and 133.81 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance exhibits weak performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing, but achieves average throughput in static web serving and Redis SET operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the B16pls_v2 offers a resource-dense ARM-based option with a burstable CPU allocation model. This makes it a viable choice for workloads with variable CPU utilization, allowing users to benefit from lower baseline costs while retaining the ability to burst to full CPU capacity. Given its 16 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, it is well-suited for multi-threaded tasks that do not require continuous peak CPU performance, such as static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations.
